title: EXP00 Web Security & Lab Architecture Quiz

questions.question: Why are Docker CPU and Memory resource limits (cgroups) enforced on lab containers?
options: To speed up internet download rates inside the container
To prevent a runaway or malicious lab process from consuming all host system resources
To allow containers to run without Docker installed
questions.explanation: Control groups (cgroups) enforce limits on memory, CPU usage, and max process IDs so an experiment cannot crash or lock up the student's host machine.

questions.question: Which command allows performing a command-line HTTP request from the attacker container to the target web server?
questions.explanation: `curl -i http://target:3000/api/status` issues an HTTP GET request to the internal DNS alias `target` on port 3000 and displays response headers.

questions.question: What happens when the student clicks 'Stop Lab' in the VLab interface?
options: The containers are paused in background memory indefinitely
All lab containers, temporary bridge networks, and volumes are safely removed to return to a clean state
The experiment source files are deleted from disk
questions.explanation: Stopping a lab triggers `docker compose down -v --remove-orphans` and label-based cleanup, purging containers, temporary networks, and volumes for a clean state.
